questions.q: Why do teams running workloads in both Azure and AWS often add Grafana rather than relying only on Azure Monitor Workbooks and CloudWatch Dashboards?
options: Azure Monitor and CloudWatch cannot store metrics for longer than 24 hours
Grafana replaces the need to ever query Azure Monitor or CloudWatch again
Native tools are cloud-specific, so an incident touching both clouds otherwise means two separate tabs and query languages instead of one view
Grafana is required by Azure and AWS before either platform will emit metrics
questions.explain: Azure Monitor and CloudWatch each only show their own cloud; Grafana sits on top as a cloud-agnostic visualization layer so one dashboard can cover both.

questions.q: What is a Grafana data source?
options: A plugin that knows how to query one specific system's real API, such as Azure Monitor or CloudWatch, and hand results back to Grafana's rendering engine
A SQL database that Grafana requires for its own internal storage
A fixed list of metric names built into Grafana core with no plugin involved
A feature exclusive to CloudWatch that Azure Monitor does not support
questions.explain: Grafana's core engine is cloud-agnostic; each data source plugin is what actually knows how to talk to one specific system's API.

questions.q: What does provisioning data sources from a YAML file (instead of the Grafana UI) achieve?
options: It makes dashboards load faster at query time
It disables authentication for the data source
It is the only way to connect more than one data source to a single Grafana instance
Data sources exist automatically the moment Grafana starts, and the config can live in source control alongside the dashboards that use it
questions.explain: Provisioning files in provisioning/datasources/ load on startup, making the setup reproducible instead of depending on someone clicking 'Add data source' by hand.

questions.q: In a dashboard panel's JSON definition, what role does the `datasource` field play?
options: It sets the visual color theme of the panel
It tells Grafana's generic rendering engine which plugin to query for that panel's data, the same role a provider's `source` field plays in Terraform
It is a legacy field with no effect in current Grafana versions
It determines how often the whole dashboard auto-refreshes
questions.explain: Each panel's datasource field selects which plugin (e.g. cloudwatch or grafana-azure-monitor-datasource) supplies that panel's data, keeping the rendering engine itself cloud-agnostic.

questions.q: What do Grafana template variables like $region let a single dashboard definition do?
options: Serve multiple environments or regions without duplicating panels, since queries re-evaluate when the dropdown value changes
Automatically translate CloudWatch metric names into Azure Monitor metric names
Bypass the need to configure a data source at all
Permanently merge two data sources into one combined data source
questions.explain: A template variable is substituted into panel queries at render time, so one dashboard can cover dev, staging, prod, or multiple regions without copy-pasting panels.
